in_hebrew.name: יסאבלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יסאבלה הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא השומר שלי' או 'אלוהים ישמור אותי'. השם נגזר מהשורש העברי 'אלישבע' שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא השומר שלי'. השם אלישבע מוזכר בתנ'ך כבתו של עמרם ואשתו של אהרון, אחיו של משה. השם יסאבלה הוא וריאציה של השם אלישבע ומשמש כנראה כמחווה לאלישבע המקראית.

in_greek.name: Υσαβέλλα
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι ο φύλαξ μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Υσαβέλλα προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα 'אלישבע' (אלישבע = Elishéva) που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ο φύλαξ μου'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Elishéva αναφέρεται στη σύζυγο του Ααρων και τη θεία του Μωυσή. Το όνομα Υσαβέλλα είναι μια παραλλαγή του ονόματος Ελισάβετ (Ελισάβετ = Elisávet) που χρησιμοποιείται στην Ορθόδοξη Εκκλησία για να τιμήσει την Ελισάβετ, τη μητέρα του Ιωάννη του Βαπτιστή.

in_latin.name: Ysabella
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ysabella derivatur ex nomine hebraeo 'אלישבע' (Elishéva), quod significat 'Deus est custos meus'. Nomen Elishéva in Biblia mentitur ut filia Amram et uxor Aaron, fratris Moysis. Ysabella est variatio nominis Elisabeth, quod in Ecclesia Catholica et Orthodoxa celebratur ut nomen sanctae Elisabeth, matris Ioannis Baptistae.

in_english.name: Ysabella
in_english.meaning: God is my protector or God is my oath
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ysabella is derived from the Hebrew name 'אלישבע' (Elishéva), which means 'God is my protector' or 'God is my oath'. It is related to the biblical name Elishéva, mentioned in the book of Exodus as the daughter of Amram and the wife of Aaron, the brother of Moses. The name Ysabella has been used in Christian tradition to honor Saint Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, and has become a popular given name among Christians, symbolizing faith, protection, and devotion to God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ysabella has a rich cultural history, with various impressions across different regions and time periods. Ysabella was a common name in the Middle Ages, appearing in many literature works, most notably as the name of the heroine in the "Cantar de Mio Cid" and as one of Shakespeare's revered characters, Isabella in "Measure for Measure." Ysabella is also linked with the Spanish royal house, as Isabella of Castile became a critical unifying figure in Spanish history, cementing the foundation of the Spanish empire during her reign.
data.spiritual_significance: For those who carry the name Ysabella, it is a profound reminder of devotion and commitment to God. The Bible reference to Elisheba in the Old Testament, bearing a child prophesied by God, serves as a powerful inspiration. Ysabella's dedication to spiritual matters is emphasized through its connection to saints like St. Isabella of Capua and St. Isabella of France, who professed exceptional religious virtues and religious devotion throughout their lives. This name underscores the importance of faith in one's personal journey and inspires the holder to live a life full of promise and dedication to God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ysabella: God's oath of devotion to El, meaning "God is my oath" or "God's promise to El," symbolizing a deep commitment to God.
